lines: Mission Control here. The launch pad lights are out and the lunar mice are throwing a party in the dark.
Your job: get one bulb glowing. We will play first and talk after.

stages.toyPrompt: Tap the switch. Watch the bulb.

1: You just closed a gap. That let electricity run round a loop, and the bulb lit up.
A loop like that is called a [[circuit]]. Break the loop and everything stops.
The [[battery]] gives the push. The [[switch]] opens and closes the gap. The [[bulb]] shows you it is working.
2: Closing the switch completed the [[circuit]], so current could flow through the [[bulb]].
The [[battery]] supplies the [[voltage]] (the push). The flow is the [[current]]. The bulb's [[resistance]] decides how much flows.
3: A [[circuit]] must be a complete conducting loop. The [[switch]] controls whether it is closed.
Conventional current leaves the + terminal of the [[battery]], passes through the [[bulb]] and returns to −. [[voltage]], [[current]] and [[resistance]] are linked by one equation, coming next.

help.1: Think of a bike chain. If the chain is joined into a loop, the wheel turns. If there is a gap, nothing moves. A circuit is the chain.
help.2: Picture a toy train track. The train only runs if the track is a full loop. Electricity is the train.
help.3: Try it yourself: tap the switch on, then off, and say out loud what changed. Closed switch, full loop, bulb on.
help.4: Watch: switch off, loop has a gap, bulb dark. Switch on, loop is complete, bulb glows. Now you do the opposite: make it dark again.

intro.1: Here is a rule that links push, flow and squeeze. It goes in your Formula Book, so you never have to remember it.
intro.2: Ohm's law links [[voltage]], [[current]] and [[resistance]]. It goes in your Formula Book.
intro.3: Ohm's law, V = IR. Rearrange it for whichever quantity you need. It goes in your Formula Book.

1: A 6 V battery pushes electricity through a part that squeezes with 2 Ω.
We want the flow. The rule: I = V ÷ R.
That makes 3 A. Three amps flow.
3: Given V = 6 V and R = 2 Ω, find I.
Rearrange V = IR to I = V ÷ R.

questions.prompt: A 9 V battery pushes electricity through a 3 Ω part. How many amps flow?

wrong.why: That is 9 × 3. We want to divide: flow = push ÷ squeeze, so 9 ÷ 3.

hints: Which rule gives flow? Look in your Formula Book.
I = V ÷ R. What are V and R here?
V is 9 and R is 3. So I = 9 ÷ 3.

help.1: Flow is push divided by squeeze. Push is 9. Squeeze is 3.
help.2: Share 9 sweets between 3 friends. Each gets the same number. That number is the answer.
help.3: Same idea, different numbers: 8 V and 2 Ω gives 8 ÷ 2 = 4 A. Now do 9 ÷ 3.
help.4: Watch: I = V ÷ R, so I = 9 ÷ 3 = 3 A. Now try 6 V through 3 Ω.

stages.title: Light the launch pad
stages.story: The pad lights are dead. Build a circuit that makes the bulb glow.

training.text: Training: the parts are already on the board. Close the switch to finish the loop.

standard.text: Build it from nothing: a battery, a switch and a bulb in one full loop, and get the bulb glowing.

stretch.text: Stretch: now light two bulbs at once. Same battery.

hints: Electricity needs a full circle. Is there a gap?
Tap the + dot on the battery, then a dot on the switch. Keep joining parts until you are back at the battery's − dot.
Battery + to the switch, switch to the bulb, bulb back to the battery −. Then close the switch.

help.1: A circuit is a loop. Join the parts in a ring, battery to switch to bulb and back to the battery.
help.2: Make a ring like a necklace. Every part is a bead and the wires are the string.
help.3: Example: battery + → switch → bulb → battery −. Then tap the switch to close it.
help.4: Tap 'Load a starter circuit' and I will have it built for you. Close the switch, then clear the board and build your own.

lines: The bulb lit because you made a full loop: battery, switch, bulb, and back.
Open the switch and the loop breaks. No loop, no flow, no light.
Next time: why an LED needs a resistor so it does not retire early.

questions.prompt: Your bulb has 20 Ω of squeeze and the battery pushes 4.5 V. How many amps flow? Give your answer to 3 decimal places, for example 0.123.
A circuit has a 12 V push and 0.5 A flows. What is the resistance in ohms?

wrong.why: That is 12 × 0.5. To find the squeeze we divide: R = V ÷ I.

hints: Rearrange V = I × R to get R.
